headline: NEW (Reuters, Oct 29 Asia date) -- Beijing 'absolutely will not' renounce force over Taiwan, TAO spokesperson says, in tougher
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] TAO spokesperson Peng Qing'en told a regular Beijing press conference that peaceful reunification under 'one country, two systems' is the fundamental approach, but: 'We absolutely will not renounce the use of force and reserve the option to take all necessary measures.'…
sources: Peng Qing'en, spokesperson for China's Taiwan Affairs Office, via Reuters
fault_line: Is Beijing's force reservation a deterrent backstop to peaceful reunification, or does the tougher tone itself raise the temperature regardless of the Xinhua reassurances?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] TAO spokesperson Peng Qing'en told a regular Beijing press conference that peaceful reunification under 'one country, two systems' is the fundamental approach, but: 'We absolutely will not renounce the use of force and reserve the option to take all necessary measures.' Reuters notes the tougher tone vs three Xinhua commentaries this week that pledged benign rule and respect for Taiwan's existing social system if it 'comes over'. Taiwan President Lai Ching-te, addressing military officers the same day, said Taiwan must demonstrate resolve to defend itself and firmly oppose annexation, aggression and unification advances. Related same-day context (CGTN, Oct 28): Beijing condemned Taiwan's DPP budgeting NT$80m (~US$2.5m) to invite US military observers to this year's and next year's Han Kuang exercises.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) reporting the TAO press conference + Taiwan presidential office comments carried in the same report. Single wire family for the statement itself; the statement's existence is the claim.
sections.what_disputed: Non-renunciation of force is decades-old standing PRC policy, not a new doctrine -- the news is the tone and timing against the Xinhua benign-rule commentaries, and top Taiwan-policy official Wang Huning's Saturday speech did not mention force at all. No new drill, mobilisation or deadline was announced in the retrieved report.
